Question_text: Fig. 1.1 shows two leaves from a holly tree. Holly leaves have sharp spines (prickles).
In the space below, construct a table of these results. Arrange the number of spines on each leaf in rank order, from lowest to highest.
Calculate the mean number of spines on the leaves growing 1 m above the ground and the mean number of spines on the leaves growing 3m above the ground.
Construct a bar chart to compare the mean number of spines on leaves growing 1m above the ground with the mean number of spines on leaves growing 3m above the ground.
Describe what the student could conclude about the number of spines on holly leaves at 1 m and 3 m above the ground.
Suggest two ways in which the reliability and validity of these conclusions could be improved.
Giving full experimental details, explain how you could compare the numbers of stomata on the upper and lower surfaces of a holly leaf.
Milk contains a reducing sugar. Explain how you could safely compare the reducing sugar contents of samples of cow's milk and goat's milk.

In the process of converting milk into cheese, an enzyme is added to the milk. Bacteria are also added. The enzyme causes solid curds to form. The solid curds are left to mature to form the cheese. An investigation was carried out into the changes in pH during the formation of cheese. The pH was measured at the start and then every week for 6 weeks.
Join the plotted points on Fig. 2.1 with ruled lines.
Using the information in Fig. 2.1, describe the changes in pH.
Suggest an explanation for the changes you have described.
